# The Celestial Gardener's Pruning

## Scripture
"I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener. He cuts off every branch in me that bears no fruit, while every branch that does bear fruit he prunes so that it will be even more fruitful." — John 15:1-2

## Reflection
When we look at the night sky, we often notice the Moon's changing phases—from slender crescent to radiant full disc and back again. But have you ever considered that the Moon never truly disappears? Even during its darkest phase, it remains faithfully orbiting Earth, hidden in shadow yet still present.

God works similarly in our lives. The "dark phases" of faith—those seasons of pruning when we feel invisible, diminished, or set apart—are not abandonment. They are the careful work of the Divine Gardener. Just as the Moon's new phase is essential for the cycle that follows, our times of spiritual pruning prepare us for greater fruitfulness.

The Moon reflects no light of its own; it shines only by the Sun's illumination. Likewise, we bear fruit only when we remain connected to Christ, the True Vine. When we feel we're in a shadow season, we can trust that the Gardener knows exactly what He's doing. He prunes not to harm but to increase our capacity for fruit that will last.

Tonight, as you observe the Moon's current phase, remember: even in your shadow seasons, you remain held in orbit by a Love that never lets go.

## Prayer
Gracious Gardener, thank You for the seasons of pruning that shape us into bearers of abundant fruit. When we feel hidden in shadow, remind us that You are still at work, and help us trust Your patient hand. Amen.
